passage: 31 December, late. Yearly sit-down with my plan tonight, tea going cold beside the laptop. Results first: passed the cloud exam, missed the team-lead role, saved less than I wanted. Then the goals. 'Lead a team by 27' is out. Honestly I liked mentoring the new joiners more than I wanted the title, so it becomes 'run the joiners' programme'. Job posts keep asking for cloud security, so that goes in as a new goal, a certificate by September. And a personal one: a proper week away with Disha, who has asked twice. I wrote a line beside every change saying why. Next December I'll read those lines before anything else. 🙂 — Thomas

qa.q: Which goal did Thomas remove from the plan?
How does Thomas feel about mentoring compared with the team-lead title?
qa.a: Thomas finds mentoring the new joiners more satisfying than the title, since Thomas admits liking it more than wanting the role.

qa.q: What could Thomas add to the yearly review to keep the plan realistic, and why?
qa.a: Thomas could ask one or two people further along in the field to read the goals, since they may notice market changes that a personal review misses.

qa.q: How might Disha see the new personal goal?
qa.a: Disha would likely feel heard, because the week away was added after Disha had asked twice. 🙂

grounding: Shows a yearly comparison of results with the plan, dropping one goal, adding others from the market and personal life, and recording the reasons.

passage:
On the last Sunday of December, in their rented house in Sangamner, Sarika spread her five-year plan on the terrace floor, weighed down with two steel glasses. Her husband, Ujjwal, brought up the tea and sat beside her.
'Every year you do this,' he said.
'Every year the world changes,' she said. She went down the list. 'Finish the B.Ed. Done. Apply for the district school post. Done, got it. Start a tuition batch in the evenings.' She paused. 'Drop this. With the baby coming in May, evenings are gone.' She crossed it out and wrote beside it: 'dropped, baby, Dec.'
Then she added one new line. 'The block office is training teachers for the new digital classrooms. I'll apply.' She wrote the reason next to it too. Ujjwal watched her fold the paper back into its plastic sleeve.

qa.q: What did Sarika write beside the crossed-out line?
How does Sarika seem to feel about crossing out the tuition batch?
qa.a: She seems calm and practical, not upset, accepting that the baby changes what her evenings can hold.

qa.q: What else could Sarika add at next year's review?
qa.a: She could note a small goal that fits life with a baby, such as one short online module, so growth continues at a gentler pace.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal see the yearly review?
qa.a: Ujjwal teases a little, but sits beside her with tea, suggesting he values the ritual and is part of it.

grounding: It shows a young woman reviewing her plan each December, dropping a goal that no longer fits, adding one based on new openings and recording why.
